table.title: [Tribal Divisions of Outer Mongolia under the Manchus, from East to West]
table.caption_extra: Outer Mongolia and Urianghai — Outer Mongolia. [Context, added by the transcriber: the divisions as they stood under the Manchu dynasty (before 1911).] Introduced: "The tribal divisions, from east to west, were as follows :—"

rows: Also known as the Eastern Division of the Khalkha Mongols. San Beise is the chief trading centre. The Kerulen valley, in this region, produces the best breed of Mongol ponies. The aimak borders on Barga on the east, Silingol on the south, and the Buriat Republic (in Siberia) on the north.
Also known as the Northern Division of the Khalkhas. In this territory stands Urga, and through it runs the great Kalgan-Urga-Kiachta caravan route. (A telegraph line follows this route.)
Also known as the Central Division of the Khalkhas. In this territory stands Uliassutai.
Also known as the Western Division of the Khalkhas.
Kobdo Special District, also known as Sain Jayagato Khan aimak

The tribes of this district are historically part of the old Western Mongol federation. They are : eleven East Wing Durbet Banners, three West Wing Durbet Banners, one East Wing and one West Wing Hoit Banner, one Jakhchin (“ Borderer ”) Banner, who are Olöts, one Olöt Banner and one Minggat Banner. There are also some Khalkha Mongols in this district, descendants of the garrisons who occupied it after the final collapse of the Western Mongol power in the eighteenth century.
